title.en: Ila Sachani: Embroidering Dreams with her Feet

text.en: Try picking up a pencil with your foot and writing your name. It is slow, tiring and needs great patience. Now imagine threading a needle and stitching tiny patterns that way. That is how Ila Sachani, a woman from Gujarat, made beautiful embroidery. Let us read her true story.

The chapter begins with Pranav M. Balasubramaniam of Palakkad in Kerala, who was born without both hands and became an artist, a singer and a para-sportsperson. You discuss how his story makes you feel and which qualities helped him succeed. Next you look at a picture of Kathiawar embroidery and think about the steps needed to make it, whether feet could do those steps, and what effort that would need.
In a tiny room in Moti Vavdi village in Bhavnagar, Gujarat, you see bright cushions, bedcovers and pillows with lovely designs. Ila Sachani, a woman with a big smile, makes them all with a shiny needle. She is very good at Kathiawar embroidery, a style that needs great skill.
Ila was born in Amreli, Gujarat, in a farmer's family. She was born with her hands hanging loose by her sides and could not use them in the usual way. Other children drew figures in the sand or plucked wild flowers. Ila wondered why she could not join them, and she wished to hold chalk and draw on a slate. Her mother and grandmother, who knew Kathiawar embroidery, were single-minded in helping her. They taught her to make beautiful patterns with her feet. It was not easy, but Ila accepted the challenge with determination. Her parents also helped her learn to do other things with her legs, such as eating and combing her hair.
Threading a needle was hard, but Ila did not give up and became an expert at a young age. Her younger brother and sister helped her. She learned many styles, even some from outside Gujarat, such as Kachhi, Kashmiri and Lucknawi. Embroidery became a way to express herself. At first she made designs for her family and friends, who were awestruck. They told others, and the village slowly discovered her skill.
The news reached a government office in Surat. Officials were moved by her story and her work and displayed samples at a state exhibition. People admired the beauty woven by her feet and bought her creations. Encouraged, she took part in exhibitions at state and national level and received many awards and honours, including the President's Medal, for her art and her willpower and creativity. The most important change was independence. She earned a regular income and found joy in doing what she loved. Her story shows that challenges can be turned into victories with focus, hard work, positivity and never giving up. Art can rise above physical boundaries and touch the soul.
Words glossed in the text are challenges, meaning difficulties; single-minded, meaning focused; determination, meaning will power; awestruck, meaning amazed; and popularity, meaning fame. The vocabulary task pairs tiny with small, wonderful with fantastic, quiet with silent, task with work, and tough with difficult. Happy and dangerous are the extra synonyms. The antonyms are tiny and huge, wonderful and terrible, quiet and noisy, task and pastime, and tough and easy.
The sentences in the text use many in you will see lots of bright colours and many lovely things. These words tell us about quantity, and here they show a large, unspecified amount. Many is used with countable nouns, such as many buses or many examples. Much is used with uncountable nouns, such as how much milk or much rice. Some and a few or a little also tell quantity. Write two sentences for each word to practise.
The listening passage is a short talk on Kathiawar embroidery. It is a very old form that uses many bright colours and many stitches, including the chain stitch. It is commonly seen on clothes and home decoration, and on clothes it appears on children's caps, ghagra skirts and men's traditional shirts. A lot of mirror work is done by fitting small mirrors along with stitches. In pairs, write two questions you would like to ask Ila Sachani.

problem.en: Choose much or many: how ____ milk, how ____ buses.

text.en: Milk cannot be counted one by one.

why.en: So we say how much milk.

text.en: Buses can be counted.

why.en: So we say how many buses.

prompt.en: Tell the story of Ila Sachani in your own words and say what it teaches us.

requiredIdeas.en: Born in a farmer's family in Amreli, Gujarat, with hands hanging loose.
Her mother and grandmother taught her Kathiawar embroidery with her feet.
Her work was shown in exhibitions and she won awards including the President's Medal.
It shows that challenges can become victories with hard work and never giving up.

commonMisconceptions.en: Ila Sachani used her hands to embroider.

points.en: Ila Sachani learned Kathiawar embroidery and did it with her feet.
Her family, especially her mother and grandmother, supported her.
Exhibitions, awards and the President's Medal made her famous and independent.
The story shows determination, focus and never giving up.
Many is for countable nouns and much is for uncountable ones.
